entries.subject: Temperature at 15 um from ten JWST MIRI visits
entries.finding: The lens. Ten MIRI/F1500W visits (program 3077's phase curve, 1177 observations 7-11, 2304 observations 1-4) reduced from raw on Bell's settings with a fractional-pixel aperture, fitted jointly with his model; the joint fit gives a dayside of 859 ppm against Bell's 797 +/- 77. On b's emission, a bare rock (T cos(z)^(1/4), nothing at night; Cowan & Agol 2011, eq. 3) fits better than the free smooth map this lens used to be: chi-squared 7002.2 against 7016.0 over 6737 samples with one parameter fewer, BIC 7099 against 7122. 497 K under the star, 485 to 510 K at one standard deviation. The smooth map spread heat onto the night side and poles, which the data do not measure. The hot-spot offset is not measured (free, 28 deg west, but only 1 in log-likelihood better than centred), so the rock is centred; north-south structure is the model's.
